theater: 高加索西麓科爾基斯平原

battle.name: 科爾基斯-斯基提亞戰爭
battle.theater: 高加索西麓科爾基斯平原
battle.brief: 公元前725年，黑海東岸的科爾基斯王國被越過高加索山脈南下的斯基提亞大軍圍困。科爾基斯人向得爾斐求問，得神諭指向金羊毛與外邦英雄伊阿宋；伊阿宋取得金羊毛後與科爾基斯人合兵，在法希斯河口擊潰圍城者。兵器卡上的亞述長矛，代表同期西高加索邊境以鐵矛、弓箭與戰車構成的軍事技術。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏤。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 公元前725年前後的黑海東岸，衝突在科爾基斯王國與越過高加索山脈南下的斯基提亞大軍之間展開。科爾基斯一方是以法希斯河（今里奧尼河）入海口為核心、以王城艾亞為中心的王國，國王埃厄忒斯出自太陽神赫利俄斯一系，宮中設有祭司階層守護阿瑞斯神廟與神聖橡樹，王弟佩爾塞斯與各地貴族、氏族首領分掌兵權；其軍隊以弓箭手與持矛步兵為主，王族與貴族乘四馬雙輪戰車，鎧甲以青銅鱗片與亞麻胸甲為主，並以黃金、白銀、穀物、造船木材與魚貨對外貿易，交好對象包括米太商人以及希臘、腓尼基的船東。斯基提亞一方在阿波羅尼奧斯的敘述中與瑪里安迪尼人一同出現，是一支由多支部族拼成的草原大軍，以弓手、輕裝騎兵與投石手為主，人數在傳統中被形容為不計其數，營地環繞城外的平原與河谷，沒有留下可考的指揮姓名，只有首領式的人物帶隊。第三方是希臘英雄伊阿宋率領的阿爾戈號遠征團，五十餘名貴族青年隨船，船上武裝齊備，另有女巫瑪狄亞隨行，實際承擔了突圍與反攻的任務。整場戰爭同時是西亞邊境體系的延伸：北方烏拉爾圖的薩杜里二世曾在744/743年兩度西征科爾基斯，亞述的鐵矛與弓箭並非本地產物，而是經由美索不達米亞的商路傳入黑海東岸。
countriesEn: Around 725 BC the clash was fought between the kingdom of Colchis on the east shore of the Black Sea and a Scythian host that came south over the Caucasus. The Colchian side was a kingdom centred on the mouth of the Phasis, the river now called the Rioni, with its royal city of Aea; it was ruled by Aeëtes of the line of Helios, and the court kept a priesthood to guard the temple of Ares and its sacred oak, while the king's brother Perses and the local nobles and clan chiefs held military authority in their own districts. Its army consisted chiefly of archers and spear-armed infantry, the royal house and the nobility rode four-horse chariots, and armour was bronze scale and linen corselet. It traded in gold, silver, grain, shipbuilding timber and fish, and kept relations with Median merchants and with Greek and Phoenician shipowners. The Scythian side appears in Apollonius of Rhodes together with the Mariandyni: a mass army assembled from several steppe tribes, formed mainly of archers, light cavalry and slingers, described in the tradition as beyond counting; it encamped in the plain and the river valleys outside the city and left no recorded names of commanders, being led only by chiefs. The third party was the expedition of Jason and the Argo, some fifty or more noble youths well armed for the voyage, with the sorceress Medea aboard, and it was they who in practice carried the counterattack. At the same time the war is an extension of the western Asian military system: Sarduri II of Urartu had campaigned twice against Colchis in 744/743 BC, and the Assyrian iron spear and the bow were not local products but reached the east Black Sea coast through the Mesopotamian trade routes.
people: 埃厄忒斯是這場戰爭的核心人物，作為太陽神赫利俄斯的孫子，他既是科爾基斯的王，也是阿瑞斯神廟與金羊毛的守護者。圍城之後他兩度派遣使者往得爾斐求問，得皮提亞的答覆是：科爾基斯的得救繫於把金羊毛獻給阿瑞斯神，並且由一位出身外邦、出身高貴的遠征者率隊而來。於是王主動把伊阿宋召來科爾基斯，卻以替我耕種龍牙、收穫時披甲作戰的艱難任務作為取羊毛的條件，等於預設他必死。伊阿宋靠女巫瑪狄亞的藥草與咒法才完成任務：他以藥膏塗抹火牛的頸部，消除火焰與恐懼，種下龍牙，收穫時出現在披甲而生的戰士之間；守護橡樹的巨龍被催眠，金羊毛才被取下。伊阿宋帶著瑪狄亞逃走之後，王宮內亂，王弟佩爾塞斯主張追擊，但科爾基斯人必須先解除圍城，於是雙方立約：伊阿宋協助對付斯基提亞人，科爾基斯人便不追擊阿爾戈號。參與的阿爾戈英雄包括阿塔蘭提斯、俄耳甫斯、阿喀琉斯、斐涅斯與提修斯等人，各有各的神話作為。圍城的斯基提亞首領在傳統中沒有留下名字，只以大王與數位族長的稱號出現。
peopleEn: Aeëtes is the central figure of the war. As a grandson of the sun god Helios he was both king of Colchis and the guardian of the temple of Ares and of the Golden Fleece. After the siege began he sent envoys twice to Delphi, and the answer of the Pythia was that the salvation of Colchis lay in bringing the Fleece to Ares and in a foreign expedition led by a man of noble birth. The king accordingly summoned Jason to Colchis himself, but made the fetching of the Fleece conditional on a task that was meant to be impossible: to plough the dragon's teeth and fight the men who grew from the crop in full armour. In effect he had arranged for the hero to die before the bargain could be kept. Jason could only complete the task with the drugs and spells of the sorceress Medea, who anointed the necks of the fire-breathing bulls so that their fire and their terror were dulled; the teeth were sown, and at the harvest Jason stood among the armed men who had sprung from them; the serpent that guarded the oak was put to sleep, and only then was the Fleece taken down. When Jason fled with Medea the court was in turmoil, and the king's brother Perses argued for pursuit, but the Colchians first had to end the siege, so a compact was made: Jason would fight the Scythians, and in return the Colchians would not pursue the Argo. Among the Argonauts were Atalanta, Orpheus, Achilles, Phineus and Theseus, each with a myth of his own. The chiefs of the besieging Scythians left no names in the tradition, appearing only as a great king and a number of tribal leaders.
kits: 兵器卡上的亞述長矛屬於公元前9世紀以來西亞邊境軍事的形制：短柄、長刃、配鐵鏃，與弓、斧及輕便的雙輪或四輪戰車配合使用，攻城時又與投石、撞槌共同構成攻城器械的骨架。這種裝備並未直接出現在科爾基斯戰場上，但它代表的技術系統確實經由美索不達米亞與高加索之間的商路進入黑海東岸，亞述與烏拉爾圖的使團、商人與掠奪者走的是同一條路。科爾基斯人自己的主力裝備是鐵鏃長矛、大小兩種弓、小圓盾與以麻布加鱗片製成的護身，投石手用石彈擲壓城牆與營壘，貴族使用四馬雙輪戰車。斯基提亞人以短弓與箭為主，配套環劍與單刃斧，長矛細而長，馬上射手用套索與標槍，鎧甲極少，靠速度與射距取勝。阿爾戈號的武裝是希臘式的：長矛與短劍、科林式圓盾、青銅或鐵製頭盔與胸甲，靠密集隊形作戰；船本身是五十支槳的近海船，吃水淺，可靠岸修補。運輸依靠皮筏、馬匹與法希斯河的水運。
kitsEn: The Assyrian spear on the card belongs to the military repertoire of the western Asian frontier from the ninth century BC: a short shaft, a long blade, an iron point, used together with the bow, the axe and light two- or four-wheeled chariots, and forming part of the frame of siege equipment alongside stone throwers and battering rams. This kit does not stand on the Colchian battlefield itself, but the system it represents did reach the east Black Sea coast along the trade routes between Mesopotamia and the Caucasus, the same road taken by Assyrian and Urartian envoys, merchants and raiders. The Colchians' own main equipment was iron-pointed spears, bows of two sizes, small round shields and body armour of linen backed with scale, with slingers throwing stones at walls and camp works, and the nobility owning four-horse chariots. The Scythians fought with short bows and arrows, ring-swords and single-edged axes, with long light spears; their mounted men used lassos and javelins, they wore almost no armour, and they relied on speed and reach. The Argo's armament was Greek in character: the long spear and the short sword, the Corinthian round shield, bronze or iron helmets and corselets, and men fought in close order. The vessel itself was a fifty-oared coastal ship of shallow draught that could be hauled up on the beach for repair. Movement of men and goods relied on rafts, pack animals and the navigable Phasis.
tactics: 這場戰爭的關鍵首先是地形。科爾基斯王城位於黑海東岸的科爾基斯平原，法希斯河與沼澤構成城區西側與南側的天然屏障，東面臨海，只有北面通往高加索山口的陸路敞開，這是圍城者能進來、卻難以四面合圍的地理原因。斯基提亞大軍在平原上展開，以弓騎輪流射擊、逼近推進、封鎖道路，再以土壘與木柵把城與外部切斷；守軍則在城牆外挖壕、堆土，抬高牆頭射界，用投石與弓弩消耗進攻者，盡量拖延到神諭指出的辦法出現。破局的方式是集中少量重裝步兵於通道：阿爾戈英雄在狹窄地帶列陣，先以長矛齊射與投擲，抵住騎兵衝鋒的正面衝力，再在兩翼以弓手與投石手支援，趁圍城軍隊拉開與隊形鬆動時反擊，把戰線壓向山口。戰後科爾基斯人沒有繼續追擊，而是立銅像紀念、為陣亡者舉行合葬與祭儀，並把金羊毛奉於阿瑞斯神廟，把盟約與戰利品的分配用儀式固定下來。
tacticsEn: The first element of this war was terrain. The royal city of Colchis stood in the Colchian plain on the east Black Sea coast, where the Phasis and the marshes formed natural barriers along the western and southern sides of the settlement, the sea lay to the east, and only the northern road towards the Caucasian passes was open. That is why the besiegers could enter yet could not close the ring on all sides. The Scythian host deployed across the plain, shooting in relays from the saddle, pressing forward and closing the roads, then cutting the city off from the outside with earthworks and timber palisades. The defenders dug ditches and raised earth outside the walls to lift the line of fire from the ramparts, met the attackers with slings and arrows to wear them down, and tried to hold out until the remedy given by the oracle could be found. The breach came from concentrating a small body of heavy infantry in a defile: the Argonauts formed up in the narrow ground, answered the cavalry charge with a massed thrust of spears and javelins, and were supported on both flanks by archers and slingers, so that when the besiegers drew out and their order loosened the counterattack could be launched and the line pushed back towards the passes. Afterwards the Colchians did not pursue: they raised a bronze image in commemoration, buried the dead together with the proper rites, hung the Fleece in the temple of Ares, and fixed the alliance and the distribution of the spoils in ceremony.
data: 可核對的數字並不多，且多數來自神話傳統而非戰報。古代名錄把阿爾戈號的英雄記為五十六人，希吉尼烏斯《神話集成》保存的清單與此相近；早期史詩《塞浦路斯史詩》則把阿爾戈號記作五十支槳的船，後世傳統改稱百槳。科爾基斯與斯基提亞雙方的軍隊人數沒有留下可靠統計，傳統只說斯基提亞大軍不計其數，這類形容不應當作數字使用。時間上，烏拉爾圖王薩杜里二世兩度西征科爾基斯是744/743年，斯基提亞與西米里安人進入黑海東岸草原的年代一般定在公元前8世紀，亦有學者依西徐·格利戈里·蘇尼的說法定在720年，戰爭列表所記的725年正落在這兩組年代之間，屬近代編年的推定而非古記。航程方面，從伊歐爾科斯經博斯普魯斯進入黑海再北上到法希斯河口，海路在1500至2000公里之間；由得爾斐陸路經安納托利亞與美索不達米亞再折向黑海東岸超過3000公里。傷亡與俘虜數字完全不見於現存材料。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are few, and most come from myth and tradition rather than from any war record. Ancient lists give fifty-six heroes for the Argo, the list preserved in Hyginus' Fabulae being close to this, while the early epic the Cypria describes the Argo as a ship of fifty oars, a later tradition raising it to a hundred. No reliable count survives for the armies of either side: the tradition says only that the Scythian host was beyond counting, a phrase that should not be used as a number. In time, the two campaigns of Sarduri II of Urartu against Colchis fall in 744/743 BC, and the arrival of the Scythians and Cimmerians in the east Black Sea steppe is generally placed in the eighth century BC, with some scholars following Ronald Grigor Suny in dating it to 720 BC; the 725 BC of the war lists falls between these two sets of dates and is a modern chronological inference rather than an ancient entry. As for distance, the sea route from Iolcus through the Bosporus into the Black Sea and then north to the mouth of the Phasis runs between 1500 and 2000 kilometres, and the land road from Delphi through Anatolia and Mesopotamia and on to the east Black Sea coast exceeds 3000 kilometres. Figures for casualties and prisoners are simply absent from the surviving material.
cause: 直接起因是科爾基斯的財富與地理位置。科爾基斯位於黑海東岸唯一適合大型商船靠岸的平原，黑海東北方的漁場、高加索的礦脈、黃金白銀與造船木材，使它成為草原部族、兩河流域商人與希臘船東都覬覦的地方。傳統敘述把衝突說成由圍城直接引發：斯基提亞大軍越過山嶺進入平原，擊敗科爾基斯的野戰部隊，把王城與耕地一併封住，屢次進攻未能得手，於是科爾基斯人向得爾斐求神諭。答案是雙重的：必須取回金羊毛、把它獻在阿瑞斯神廟，並且要有一位外邦英雄率軍來援，兩者缺一不可。國王接到神諭後的反應極具算計：他以款待伊阿宋為名把這位英雄引進國土，卻用幾乎不可能完成的耕種龍牙任務作為交換，等於要他在完成之前就死於火牛與骨刺之間。於是三方在王城之外的狹窄口子上撞在一起：遠征者要取金羊毛，國王要外邦人的性命，圍城者要科爾基斯的土地與財富。
causeEn: The immediate cause was the wealth and the position of Colchis. The kingdom lay on the only stretch of plain on the east Black Sea coast suitable for large merchant shipping, and the fishing grounds of the north-eastern sea, the mineral veins of the Caucasus, its gold and silver and its shipbuilding timber made it a prize for steppe tribes, for merchants of Mesopotamia and for Greek shipowners alike. The tradition presents the conflict as directly caused by the siege: the Scythian host came over the mountains into the plain, defeated the Colchian field army, shut up the royal city together with the farmland, and failed to take the city by repeated assault, so the Colchians sent to Delphi for an oracle. The answer was twofold: the Fleece had to be brought back and hung in the temple of Ares, and a foreign hero had to lead an expedition to the rescue; neither part would do without the other. The king's response to the oracle was calculated: he drew Jason into the country under the pretext of hospitality and made the Fleece conditional on a task that was very nearly impossible to perform, the ploughing of the dragon's teeth, which amounted to ordering his death among the bulls and the men who grew from the bones. Thus three parties collided in the narrow gap outside the royal city: the expedition wanted the Fleece, the king wanted the stranger's life, and the besiegers wanted the land and the treasure of Colchis.
impact: 從神話層面看，這場戰爭為整個西方文明提供了一條通往黑海東岸的敘事通道：阿爾戈號遠征從此成為希臘人首次進入黑海的框架，希臘世界後來在法希斯、提亞斯一帶設立的商站與殖民點，都以金羊毛的航線作為理由與根據。從物質層面看，圍城者退去之後，科爾基斯的黃金、白銀、鐵料與奴隸進入地中海的交換網絡，阿爾戈號帶回歐洲的金羊毛在後世被附會成冶金、染色與黃金價值的來源，阿爾戈諸神的祭禮也隨之傳播到希臘與南義大利的港口。從歷史層面看，斯基提亞與西米里安人的南遷把南高加索拖入鐵器時代列強的角力：烏拉爾圖的薩杜里二世西征、阿開美尼德後來把拉茲卡設為行省、羅馬的蓬提斯將軍對該區的經營，都可以看作這場圍城後半個多世紀的餘波。母題上，外邦英雄解除蠻族圍城的模式，後來在希臘人對黑海北岸的想像中不斷被重複。
impactEn: At the level of myth, this war gave the whole western world a narrative road to the east Black Sea coast: the voyage of the Argo became the frame for the first Greek entry into the Black Sea, and the trading posts and colonies the Greek world later set up around the Phasis and at Dioscurias appealed to the route of the Fleece as their warrant. At the material level, once the besiegers withdrew, the gold, silver, iron and slaves of Colchis entered the exchange networks of the Mediterranean, the Fleece carried back to Europe was later identified as the source of metallurgy, of dyeing and of the value of gold, and the cults of the Argonauts spread with it to the harbours of Greece and southern Italy. At the historical level, the southward movement of the Scythians and Cimmerians pulled the southern Caucasus into the rivalry of the iron age powers: the campaigns of Sarduri II of Urartu, the later establishment of Lazica as a satrapy under the Achaemenids, and the Roman administration of the region under the generals of Pontus can all be read as the long aftermath of the siege. At the level of the motif, the pattern of a foreign hero lifting a siege laid by barbarians was repeated endlessly in later Greek imaginings of the northern Black Sea.
result: 以現存材料而言，結局是科爾基斯得救而圍城者退走。伊阿宋一行按約定與科爾基斯人合兵，在城外的平原與山口之間擊潰斯基提亞大軍，對方退回北方高原，聯盟依誓約不再追擊阿爾戈號；科爾基斯人立起銅像與紀念柱，為陣亡者舉行合葬與祭儀，並依神諭把金羊毛懸於阿瑞斯神廟的橡樹上。伊阿宋與瑪狄亞隨後從科爾基斯東岸登船遠逃，佩爾塞斯率領的追兵一度逼近，最終雙方各自散去，這場圍城戰爭在傳統中沒有留下追擊戰的記錄。需要說明的是，這場戰爭的歷史幾乎全部出自阿波羅尼奧斯·羅迪烏斯《阿爾戈號紀事》（公元前3世紀）第三、四卷，以及後世對維吉爾的註釋等衍生材料；所謂公元前725年，是把神話事件與亞述與烏拉爾圖的西征及西米里安與斯基提亞南遷的年代相對齊之後的近代推定，具體月份、交戰地名、雙方兵員與損耗數字均無可考，戰爭列表因此只能按單一年度收錄。
resultEn: On the evidence that survives, the outcome was the relief of Colchis and the withdrawal of the besiegers. Jason and his companions fought alongside the Colchians as agreed and broke the Scythian host in the plain and among the passes outside the city; the enemy withdrew towards the northern highlands, and by the terms of the compact the Colchians did not pursue the Argo. The Colchians raised a bronze image and a commemorative column, buried their dead with the proper rites, and, as the oracle had required, hung the Fleece on the oak in the temple of Ares. Jason and Medea then put out to sea from the eastern shore of Colchis; the pursuing force of Perses came close for a time, but the two parties finally dispersed, and the tradition records no battle of pursuit from this siege. It should be said that the history of this war comes almost entirely from the third and fourth books of the Argonautica of Apollonius of Rhodes, written in the third century BC, and from later derivative material such as the scholia on Virgil; the date 725 BC is a modern inference made by aligning the mythic event with the campaigns of Assyria and Urartu in the west and the southward movement of the Cimmerians and Scythians. The precise months, the place of the fighting, the numbers engaged on both sides and the losses are simply not recoverable, which is why the list of wars can only record the conflict as a single year entry.
